coach_briefing: The reconstructed session matches the planned six-work-interval structure, with all recoveries within the 3–5 minute prescription. SPM execution was compliant in work intervals 1–4 and 6; work-05 was a real rate deviation at 19.99 SPM versus 22–24 prescribed. Speed was highest in work-04 (3.459 m/s), then lower in work-05 (2.970 m/s) and work-06 (3.168 m/s). A tailwind-to-headwind shift occurred around 1800 s and is time-aligned with the later slower work, but it is not proof of causation. Distance-target completion and resistance-band use remain unknown.

deviations.description: Average SPM was 19.99 against the prescribed 22–24 SPM range for the fifth work interval.

limitations: Time alignment supports association only; it does not establish that wind caused the speed changes or that athlete performance regressed.
environment_assessment.summary: Effective conditions changed from a 1.0 m/s tailwind at session start (effective headwind -1.0 m/s) to a 5.5 m/s headwind, with sign change at 1800 s. This overlaps the later work intervals, including reduced speed in work-05 and work-06 relative to work-04.

follow_up_questions: Did the crew use the resistance band for work intervals 1–3 and remove it before interval 4?
Was there a deliberate reason for holding approximately 20 SPM during work interval 5 rather than the prescribed 22–24 SPM?

prescribed_blocks: 3 x 1 km at 19–21 SPM, resistance band, 180–300 s active recovery
3 x 1 km at 22–24 SPM, no resistance band, 180–300 s active recovery
plan_summary.summary: Planned water session: 6 x 1 km with 3–5 minutes active recovery; first three work intervals at 19–21 SPM with a resistance band, then three at 22–24 SPM without it.

session_associations.reason: The recordings spatially match despite a 37-second start-clock offset; route evidence supports a single outing, while the clock conflict remains unresolved.
